newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea expects N.Korea to meet on peace talks.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea expects N.Korea to meet on peace talks.

text.p: North Korea is expected to agree to a meeting of senior officials with the United States and South Korea to arrange four-nation peace talks, a South Korean foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday.

Spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung told Reuters that progress had been made in working-level discussions among the three countries in New York recently and South Korea was "cautiously optimistic" over the prospects of holding peace talks this year.
The four-nation talks, also involving China, are aimed at working out a peace settlement to replace a now-fraying armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
Lee said working-level officials from the United States and the two Koreas had met five times since May 30. "There's been slow but positive progress," he added.

He said he expected senior officials to meet "within the next couple of months" to discuss the agenda for the four-nation talks. North Korea in April agreed in principle to join four-nation peace talks but made its participation conditional on large-scale food aid and an easing of U.S. trade sanctions.
